lines.speaker: stonekeeper
lines.text: Mind the verge, it goes soft this time of year and the stone does not, so you will go over.

lines.speaker: stonekeeper
lines.text: You are the one from the monastery. I can tell, because you are reading the names and not the plaque. Everyone reads the plaque.

lines.speaker: stonekeeper
lines.text: Four hands cut these. The first was Ade's — Captain Ade, in the week after, and she got eleven down before her own name went on it and somebody else had to pick up the chisel. Then Bern, then Bern's daughter Ysolt, then me. I have had it forty years.

lines.speaker: stonekeeper
lines.text: Two hundred and six. They came down off the Ash Camp with steel nobody could account for, and they held that wall for a winter, and the Board took the valley in the spring anyway.

lines.speaker: stonekeeper
lines.text: Two hundred and six. They held the wall for a winter, and it was the winter the charter got out, and there are people who will tell you those two facts are unrelated.

lines.speaker: stonekeeper
lines.text: Nobody knows who gave it to them. The story says an auditor, which is the sort of thing people say when the truth has no shape they can hold on to.

lines.speaker: stonekeeper
lines.text: An auditor. Down a mountain. With a ledger, presumably, and a very sharp pencil.

lines.speaker: stonekeeper
lines.text: You have gone a colour. Sit down on the stone, it does not mind, it has had worse. Everybody who reads the whole thing through sits down eventually.
